decisionContext.lockedTarget: Causal determination by factors beyond control prevents the sourcehood required for responsibility.

components.text: Responsibility in the required sense demands that the agent be the appropriate source of action.
An action causally determined by factors beyond the agent's control lacks that appropriate sourcehood.

route.description: Show that luck and factors beyond the agent's control defeat the sourcehood needed for basic-desert responsibility while leaving forward-looking responses available.
route.successCriteria: The route succeeds if agents are shown not to be appropriate sources for basic desert and safety, rehabilitation, or rule enforcement can replace retributive blame and punishment.

bridges.description: Basic-desert moral responsibility and retributive blame or punishment are unwarranted, even if independently justified forward-looking responses remain.
Who agents are and what they do result from luck or factors beyond their control, so they lack the appropriate sourcehood for basic desert.
Reasons-responsive distinctions, sanctions, safety restrictions, rehabilitation, and rule enforcement can be retained on non-desert forward-looking grounds.
Adding physical indeterminacy does not let the agent settle which outcome occurs and therefore cannot rescue basic-desert control.
